name: Mewing tongue-to-palate full suction hold

lead: Mewing is a tongue-posture practice named after orthodontist John Mew, in which the tongue rests against the roof of the mouth. The full suction hold is a variant that tries to seal the entire tongue, not just its tip or front, against the palate.
Practitioners do it hoping for a more defined jawline and better facial support over time. Mewing generally is described by sources as unproven; no published study has tested this specific variant.

paras: It is a posture held through the day with no equipment, usually while keeping the lips closed. Practitioners differ on how much pressure and how much of the tongue should touch the palate, and the full suction hold is the version that emphasizes the whole tongue.
No specific harms are documented for this variant. Wikipedia reports that the American Association of Orthodontists states there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw.

chain: Whole tongue held against the palate
Claimed sustained pressure on the upper jaw
Claimed more forward, defined facial structure
angle.text: Practitioners hold the tongue sealed against the palate hoping the resting posture supports jaw and facial structure over time. Where mewing is concerned, the claimed benefit is a more defined jaw and midface.

lead: Mewing is an oral posture practice in which the tongue rests against the roof of the mouth with some pressure; proponents say this can reshape the jaws and face. It is named after British orthodontist John Mew, who developed it with his son Mike as part of orthotropics.[1]

The tongue-to-palate full suction hold is a variant that aims to seal the whole tongue against the palate. Practitioners adopt it hoping that the more complete contact gives a stronger effect on jaw and midface development, which they associate with a more defined appearance. This variant has no separate published research; discussion of mewing as a whole is covered below.

paras: In standard mewing, the tongue rests against the roof of the mouth. In the full suction variant, practitioners describe sealing the whole tongue to the palate, as if by suction. The distinction is one of degree, how much of the tongue is involved, within the same posture practice.[1]

Mewing comes from orthotropics, developed by John Mew and his son Mike.[1] Interest began rising in January 2019 and the practice went viral on social media, notably in incel and looksmaxxing subcultures.[1][2] Mewing is typically classed as softmaxxing, a low-intensity method.[2]

Wikipedia states that no credible scientific research has shown orthotropics to be effective, that most orthodontists do not regard mewing as an alternative to jaw surgery, and that the American Association of Orthodontists says there is no evidence it improves the jaw.[1] Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024.[1] Practitioners continue to report their own perceived changes.

timeline.event: Interest in mewing begins rising and spreads on social media.[1]
Mike Mew is struck from the UK dental register.[1]
